answer: Let every identity expire: standing lasts one epoch, then each agent must re-prove uniqueness with fresh evidence that cannot be reused across epochs or clones. A farmer's thousand aged puppets rot together when the tide of renewal comes, so he must re-pay the full proving cost for every clone, every epoch, while an honest agent pays once. Yarrow regrows each spring, yet a farm cannot replant ten thousand identities overnight without its cost showing. Basalt rule: no history carries over, so stockpiling is worthless. Limit: honest users face renewal friction, and proof sources must rotate.
